title: Dynamic weight reservation and KV pressure forecasting for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching is enabled across multi-tenant pools, we observe tail latency spikes and OOMs caused by unpredictable KV cache growth and transient activation peaks. Existing static headroom allocations (fixed percent per worker) either waste GPU memory for smaller models or cause OOMs for larger models under burst traffic. We need a system-level GPU memory budgeting approach that dynamically reserves weight and KV/activation headroom per model and per worker based on short-term pressure forecasts and a conservative safety margin.

Goal: Build a forecasting-driven memory budgeter that: (1) models memory usage across weights, KV cache, and activations for active model versions, (2) forecasts short-window KV pressure and activation growth from request traces, (3) applies a dynamic "weight reservation" abstraction to ensure weights are pinned yet allow temporary soft-eviction of lower-priority KV when headroom is required, (4) exposes headroom signals to autoscaler and scheduling components, and (5) adds simulation and CI checks to prevent regressions in allocation policies.

Scope: This ticket covers design, runtime prototype in our serving runtime, integration tests, and a small Console metric surface for headroom per route. Follow-up tickets will cover full rollout, dedicated mode tuning, and tenant-configurable policies.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implements a memory estimator that reports weight_bytes, kv_bytes, activation_bytes and total_bytes per model instance on GPU
Forecasting component consumes recent request trace (1-5 minute window) and emits KV growth probability and expected activation percentile for the next 60s
Runtime enforces a dynamic reservation: reserve_weight_bytes + soft_headroom_bytes where soft_headroom can be reclaimed from low-priority KV entries with LRU score and age cutoff
No regressions: baseline 99th percentile latency increase < 5% on internal perf tests for continuous batching workloads compared to current canary
Add end-to-end integration test that simulates KV storm (rapid long-generation requests) and demonstrates soft-eviction preventing OOMs with <2% failed requests
Console shows per-route headroom metric and an annotation with active forecast and reclaimed_kv_bytes for at least one test route
design_notes: Memory model: treat weights as resident static_cost, KV as elastic cache_cost, activations as transient peak_cost. Use per-layer fanout estimates to approximate activation growth given sequence_length and batch_size.
Forecasting: implement lightweight exponential moving average + burst detector for KV churn; fallback to conservative preset when trace is insufficient.

Reservation semantics: reserve_weight_bytes is strict. soft_headroom_bytes is a sliding pool that the runtime may reclaim from marked low-priority KV entries using an async eviction path to avoid blocking critical token generation.
Priority model: mark KV entries with route_priority, last_access_ts, token_prefix_length to prefer evicting long-unused caches from background routes.
Safety margin: default safety_multiplier = 1.15 applied to forecasted peak to avoid oscillation; make tenant-configurable in dedicated/private modes.
Integration points: expose headroom signal to scheduler, autoscaler, and the canary rollback policy; add metric hooks for tracing and Grafana dashboards.
tasks: Implement memory estimator module in runtime (C++): calculate weights, kv, activation bytes per model instance
Add simple forecast engine (go) that reads recent request logs and emits per-worker short-term KV pressure
Implement soft-eviction path in KV manager and LRU scoring changes to support priority-tagged evictions
Wire reservation enforcement into allocation path that decides accept/queue/reject for incoming batch requests
Create synthetic load test harness that simulates multi-route continuous batching with mixed seq lengths
Add integration test that verifies no OOMs and metrics emission under KV storm
Add Console metric surface and a debug endpoint returning current reservation and forecast
Docs: internal README explaining reservation knobs and failure modes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive soft-eviction could degrade quality for long-running sessions. Mitigation: evict only entries older than min_ttl and preserve entries with high reuse score.
Risk: forecast underestimates rare bursts leading to OOM. Mitigation: safety_multiplier and fast-fail fallback that rejects very large batches when headroom is below absolute min_threshold.
Risk: added CPU overhead for forecasting and eviction scanning. Mitigation: sampling-based scans and rate-limited forecasting; move heavy checks to background threads.
Risk: multi-tenant fairness when one tenant spikes. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant soft limits and expose tenant_quota_exceeded events for autoscaler to react.
